bezier-patch-trail.alt: A curved, untextured trail formed by a small number of smooth Bézier patches.
bezier-patch-trail.caption: A trail starts as a connected strip of curved patches. Its corners and edges define the shape before any textures are added.

cage-control-snow-overhangs.alt: Magenta control-cage points shaping a rounded snow overhang above a rock wall.
cage-control-snow-overhangs.caption: Control cages expose the handles behind the surface. Here, they shape a snow lip that extends beyond the rock face.

course-definition.alt: Scene Mode with a green course line, editable knots, and course settings beside a snowy turn.
course-definition.caption: Scene → Course: the green knots describe the course route. Selecting a knot exposes its position, width, and checkpoint settings.

course-speed-profiles.alt: A snowy course shaded by predicted speed, with a color key and a warning about the course start being off the terrain.
course-speed-profiles.caption: Predicted speed is a diagnostic, not a completed test run. This capture also shows a start-position warning that should be fixed before trusting the prediction.

custom-map.alt: A developing custom mountain in Edit mode with connected patches, cliffs, a narrow route, and untextured terrain.
custom-map.caption: A course in progress: build the route and the surrounding landforms together, then refine the transitions between them. Earlier interface shown.

custom-props.alt: Props Mode with a custom pirate-ship model on the snow and a searchable library of custom models.
custom-props.caption: The Custom prop library collects your own models. Pick a model, place it on the mountain, and adjust its transform.

edge-loops.alt: A selected yellow edge chain with weld, bridge, crease, smooth, and control-cage actions in the Edit panel.
edge-loops.caption: An edge selection makes local topology and shaping actions available. The panel tells you which operations apply to the current selection.

effects-editor.alt: Effects Mode with a selected fireworks trigger, an effect list, a Preview effect control, and individual effect nodes.
effects-editor.caption: An imported-course inspection example: select the host prop, choose its effect, then inspect the nodes and preview the behavior.

integrating-trail-with-terrain.alt: Two textured trail ribbons running beside a raised terrain block in Edit Mode.
integrating-trail-with-terrain.caption: The trail ribbon and the mountain body are separate surfaces at this stage. Review their intersections and connect the edges deliberately.

map-editing.alt: The Slopesmith Paint Mode workspace showing a snowy mountain, the right-side palette, and the bottom Texture Library.
map-editing.caption: The working layout: modes across the top, the mountain in the center, selection tools on the right, and the asset library along the bottom.

map-texturing.alt: A terrain patch painted with an ice tile, with the paint palette and imported-course Texture Library visible.
map-texturing.caption: Paint applies a tile to a terrain patch. This earlier interface capture shows an imported texture library; your available tiles depend on your project and local imports.

maya-research.alt: A Maya 3.0 research session showing a curved lofted surface in four viewports.
maya-research.caption: Behind the scenes: a Maya 3.0 surface-modeling research session. Maya is not required to use Slopesmith.

multilane-trail-junctions.alt: A branching trail network with one selected path and controls for target width, lanes, length, and center dish.
multilane-trail-junctions.caption: Trail Shape controls the ribbon’s cross-section and patch layout. Shared path points form the junction between routes.

patch-editing.alt: A close view of a patch network showing curved edges and connected corner points.
patch-editing.caption: The visible patch edges are curves. Moving a corner or changing a handle affects the smooth surface between the points.

play-testing.alt: An early Slopesmith test ride on unfinished terrain with surface colors and a rider in view.
play-testing.caption: Test the route while it is still simple. This development capture shows an earlier Play interface; the current workflow uses Test mode.

prop-placement.alt: Trees placed near the inside of a snowy turn, with the terrain’s patch edges visible.
prop-placement.caption: Use props to frame a corner and communicate scale. Keep the rider’s approach and landing visible as you add scenery.

surface-types.alt: A course in surface-type view with color-coded terrain and a legend for snow, powder, ice, and other ride surfaces.
surface-types.caption: The surface overlay reveals the assigned ride types. The color key explains the terrain’s behavior even when textures hide those boundaries.

texture-palette.alt: A texture palette containing aligned snow, ice, rock, and turn-marker tiles, with an orange seam indicator.
texture-palette.caption: Arrange related tiles next to one another in a palette. Orange edge markers call attention to tile edges that do not align.

wireframe-diagram.alt: A wireframe overview showing the course terrain, trees, props, and effect markers.
wireframe-diagram.caption: Wireframe gives another way to read a busy scene: the terrain network, prop geometry, and effect markers can be inspected together.
